name: OpenAISearchDetail
title: GPT-5 Search Detail
description: Answer one question from a tree of rows by opening one branch at a time: each turn reads the choices one step from the rows it opened, and the model opens more or answers, with the path it took and the words each answer rests on.
whenToUse: Pick when the answer to one question sits somewhere inside a large object (a deal and its documents, a long document and its sections, a table's rows) and sending the whole of it to a model would be too long or too costly: the model reads titles and descriptions to choose where to go, and reads text only where it chose to. The wrong choice when the content is already short enough to hand over whole, or when many questions are asked of one text at once. Wire the question and the ids to start from in as inputs.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.description: The ids to start from, comma-separated (one to five), such as the row the caller holds

outputs.name: answer
outputs.description: The answer, or null when the walk found none

outputs.name: sources
outputs.description: What the answer rests on, each with its id, its pages and the exact words

outputs.name: path
outputs.description: Every turn in order, what was opened, what was chosen next and why. The lineage of the answer

outputs.name: caveat
outputs.description: When another document may give a different answer, which one and what may differ; null when none may

outputs.name: stopped
outputs.description: Why the walk ended, until (answered or gave up), maxTurns or stuck

model.title: Model
model.description: GPT-5.6 model that chooses where to go and answers

instructions.title: Instructions
instructions.description: How to walk and when to stop. The default is written for any tree; add to it only what is particular to the questions this node will be asked.
instructions.default: You answer one question by walking a tree of rows, one step at a time. Each turn you are shown the rows you opened. Each row has its own face (title, description, whenToUse) and its choices: what it belongs to (up), what is inside it (down), and what sits beside it (sideways), each with an id, a title, a description, a whenToUse and pages. A row may also carry found: the parts anywhere under it whose faces best match the question, each with its id and how near it came: a hint at which row to look in, never the list of what is there. At the bottom of the tree a row also carries its words: text, or a table's rows. Choose the ids to open next, at most five, only from ids you have been shown. Open every one that could hold the answer, up to five, never the fewest. A found part names the row worth looking in: open THAT ROW and read what is inside it (down), because found ranks faces by wording and the words of a question are rarely the words of a title. Then open the parts it names. You have not answered from a row until you have read its own words, and you may never say a row does not hold something until you have seen what is inside it. You do not see earlier turns again: keep in your notes what you found, where, and the ids still worth opening. Answer only from text or rows you have read, never from a title alone, and give every source: its id, its pages, and the exact words the answer rests on. Open nothing only when you are answering. When the rows give more than one answer (for different variants, dates or sources), give each, labelled with the row it comes from and its pages, and never choose one silently: whoever asked decides which applies. Before answering, check the other found parts that could hold a different answer. If nothing read holds the answer and nothing left to open looks likely to, answer null and open nothing.

maxTurns.title: Most turns
maxTurns.description: The most branches opened in a row before the walk stops without an answer. The platform stops every walk at 20, whatever this says.

reasoning.title: Reasoning
reasoning.description: How much the model thinks before each choice.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: openai
package.packageFile:
# The package envelope, and now the ONLY envelope: this package is fully
# declarative. All five nodes are manifests, there is no src/ and no package.json,
# so nothing here is built, published or imported. The retired TypeScript sits at
# _legacy/nodes/openai for reference.
#
# A code node of the same type always beats a manifest at load, which is what made
# migrating one node at a time possible. With the code gone there is nothing left
# to beat these.

name: openai
displayName: OpenAI
description: OpenAI integration for Unoverse
version: 1.3.0
category: ai
# First-party. The marketplace shows this on every node the package registers, so
# "who am I trusting with this credential" is answerable without leaving the screen.
publisher: unoverse
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749262616/gravity/icons/ChatGPT-Logo.svg.webp

features:
  - GPT-5.6 models
  - Live two-way voice, with the model interruptible mid-sentence
  - Streaming responses
  - Function/tool calling
  - Text embeddings
  - Structured JSON output
  - Vision (image inputs)
  - Realtime voice calls with transcripts of both sides
  - Search detail, one question answered by opening one branch of a tree at a time

# The ONLY hosts this package's nodes may call. The executor refuses anything else.
#
# A manifest cannot execute code, but without this it could still say "send this
# credential to evil.example", which is exfiltration with no code at all. One short
# reviewable list is what makes a manifest safe to accept from someone else.
allowedHosts:
  - api.openai.com
  # LOOPBACK, numeric form: OpenAISearchDetail reads the choices one step from a row from the
  # platform's own engine over `scope.engineUrl` (127.0.0.1:4101), the same declaration the
  # ingest and spatial packages carry. It sends the engine ids, never the credential.
  - 127.0.0.1

# Executor capabilities every manifest node here depends on. Deploy REFUSES this
# package if the target universe's executor cannot satisfy them, so a manifest can
# never name a capability that only exists on a newer executor.
# `ws` and the raised floor came with OpenAIRealtimeVoice (2026-08-12): a realtime session is a
# SOCKET, and the duplex runtime that holds one open landed in executor 1.5.0.
requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [sse, json, ws]
  # OpenAIAgent keeps its OpenAI conversation id between runs. A universe whose executor
  # cannot do this would otherwise read a permanently cold cache and start a new
  # conversation every turn: memory that silently never remembers.
  state: [read, merge]
  # OpenAISearchDetail walks in turns (`repeat`), each built from the reply before.
  repeat: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.5.0"

credentials.openAICredential.yaml:
# The SHAPE of the credential, never its value. Transcribed from
# plugin-base/src/credentials/openai.ts, which this package re-exports today.
#
# Values live where they already live: encrypted in Postgres on a deployed universe,
# and in the developer's own .env locally. That is why a manifest is safe to commit.
#
# Nodes reference this by NAME. At run time context.credentials holds EVERY credential
# in the workflow keyed by name, and the executor must select by name, never by
# scanning for the first object with an apiKey: openAICredential, apolloCredential,
# hunterCredential and searchapiCredential all expose one, so a scan silently
# authenticates against the wrong service the moment a second is added to the
# workflow (04-credentials.md).

name: openAICredential
displayName: OpenAI
description: Credentials for OpenAI API
documentationUrl: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your OpenAI API key
    placeholder: sk-...

  - name: organizationId
    displayName: Organization ID
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Your OpenAI organization ID (optional)
    placeholder: org-...

  - name: baseUrl
    displayName: Base URL
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Custom API endpoint (optional)
    default: https://api.openai.com/v1

shared.endpoints.yaml:
# OpenAI's endpoints. Written once here rather than seven times across the nodes.
#
# No chat/completions: every node uses the Responses API. `messages` is the legacy shape.
#
#   url: { $ref: ../../shared/endpoints.yaml#/responses }

responses: https://api.openai.com/v1/responses
embeddings: https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings

# A CONVERSATION is OpenAI's own server-side memory: a durable id you mint once and then
# name on every response. Items are prepended to the request and the turn's input and
# output are appended back, so history never travels from here and is never stored here.
# Minted with POST and an empty body; the reply carries the id.
#
# NO CALLER SINCE 2026-08-23. OpenAIAgent was the only one and now chains with
# previous_response_id instead. Kept because the URL is a fact about the vendor rather
# than about any node, and re-deriving it is the sort of small cost that argues for
# leaving a one-line constant alone. Nothing here decides which mechanism a node uses —
# each declares that next to its own reason (shared/tools.yaml).
conversations: https://api.openai.com/v1/conversations
shared.models.yaml:
# The canonical GPT model list, the SINGLE source every OpenAI node references,
# organised by TIER. Transcribed from src/shared/models.ts.
#
# Models come in three tiers. A new generation is a one-line edit per tier here, and
# every node plus every saved workflow moves over automatically.
#
# The DATA lives here. The FALLBACK LOGIC (resolveModel: a retired id resolves to the
# current best model in its tier, so replacing a generation cannot break a saved
# workflow) is computation, not description, so it belongs to the executor. It is
# declared per config field as `resolver: modelTier`, not written here.

# One current model per tier. Update these three lines when a new generation ships.
byTier:
  small: gpt-5.6-luna # cost-optimized, high-volume
  medium: gpt-5.6-terra # balanced intelligence/cost, the default
  large: gpt-5.6 # frontier, complex work

# Balanced middle tier, the sensible default for most work.
default: gpt-5.6-terra

# The NARRATOR: the model that writes an agent's short "thinking" status line. A separate
# concern from the model doing the work, so it is named separately.
#
# Deliberately NOT the 5.6 family: 5.6 is luna/sol/terra with no nano tier, and this call
# exists to reach the user fast, not to be clever. Measured 2026-07-26, three runs each,
# same prompt and schema:
#
#   gpt-5.4-nano   avg 1137ms   [1470, 905, 1035]
#   gpt-5.6-luna   avg 2043ms   [1846, 2337, 1945]
#
# Luna is ~80% slower and less consistent for lines that are indistinguishable in quality.
# Re-measure when a faster small model ships; never assume.
narrator: gpt-5.4-nano


# The picker's options. Listed large first so the strongest reads first.
enum:
  - gpt-5.6
  - gpt-5.6-terra
  - gpt-5.6-luna

enumNames:
  - Sol (Frontier, complex work)
  - Terra (Balanced intelligence/cost)
  - Luna (Cost-optimized, high-volume)
shared.realtimeTools.yaml:
# The OpenAI REALTIME tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does not belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it does not
# belong copied into a node either. It belongs here, exactly as `openai/shared/tools.yaml` holds the
# Responses protocol — imported whole:
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#
# WHY THIS IS NOT `openai/shared/tools.yaml`. Same vendor, different API, and three real differences
# rather than cosmetic ones:
#
#   the call event   Responses says `response.output_item.done` and needs a `when` to tell a function
#                    call from any other completed item. Realtime has a dedicated
#                    `response.function_call_arguments.done`, so no `when` is needed.
#   offer, not      Responses puts the tool list in each REQUEST, so a list that GREW since the
#   toolsInto       last turn is re-sent for free and there is nothing to declare. A socket sends
#                   it once at the handshake, so growth has to be announced on purpose — which is
#                   what `offer` below is. Same fact, two shapes: `toolsInto` names a request
#                   field, `offer` names a whole message.
#   no continuity    Responses chains turns with previous_response_id. THE SOCKET IS THE CONTINUITY:
#                    the conversation never ended, so there is nothing to chain.
#
# Also absent, and deliberately: `maxTurns` and `stuckAfterRepeats`. Both count turns, and a turn is
# one model call. Nothing to count here. What bounds a runaway session is the executor's own idle and
# duration ceiling.

# How ONE tool is offered. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters }

# HOW THE LIST IS RE-OFFERED once it has grown. `tools` is the whole live list, already in the
# envelope `tool` above produces.
#
# ONLY `tools`: session.update MERGES (verified live 2026-08-12), so instructions, modalities,
# voice and turn detection survive untouched. Re-sending the whole session block would be a second
# copy of the handshake, free to drift. Safe at any moment — the vendor gates `response.create` on
# an idle conversation, never session.update.
offer: >-
  return { type: 'session.update', session: { type: 'realtime', tools: tools } }

# HOW THE INSTRUCTIONS ARE RE-SENT when a region skill comes into force or is cleared.
#
# The same shape and the same reason as `offer` above, for the other thing the handshake sent
# once. A request/response vendor rebuilds its prompt every turn, so a skill absorbed on one
# turn is in the next request for free and there is nothing to declare. A socket sent
# `instructions` at the handshake and would otherwise never mention it again, so the model
# would keep working to a prompt that no longer describes where the conversation is.
#
# ONLY `instructions`: session.update MERGES, so voice, modalities, tools and turn detection
# survive untouched. `skillsText` is the platform's rendering of what is in force — it decides
# WHICH skills apply, this decides where the vendor puts them.
#
# The config prompt is repeated rather than sent alone, because a merge REPLACES the field it
# names: sending only the skills would drop the role the node was configured with.
reinstruct: >-
  return { type: 'session.update',
           session: { type: 'realtime',
                      instructions: config.systemPrompt + skillsText } }

# How a call ARRIVES. `match` is what makes a stream tractable: events keep coming for the whole
# conversation, and this says which of them is a tool call rather than a transcript or audio.
call:
  match: response.function_call_arguments.done
  id: "return response.call_id"
  name: "return response.name"
  # A JSON STRING, which the executor parses. The trap the schema warns about: passed through
  # unparsed, the tool receives a string where it expected its parameters.
  arguments: "return response.arguments"

# How the result goes BACK. TWO messages, because OpenAI separates them: the output joins the
# conversation, then a response is asked for. Without the second the model holds the result silently.
result: >-
  return [
    { type: 'conversation.item.create',
      item: { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output } },
    { type: 'response.create' }
  ]
shared.task.yaml:
# THE TASK A CALL WAS GIVEN, FOUND RATHER THAN NAMED.
#
# A voice node is wired to whatever the canvas put upstream, so it cannot know the sending
# node's id or the name of the output handle. What it does know is the SHAPE: a task carries a
# list of `fields` still outstanding. So every wired value is looked at and the one with that
# shape is the task.
#
# THREE LEVELS, because a wired input arrives nested and how deep depends on the wiring:
# `signal.<input handle>.<sending node>.<its output>`. Measured 2026-09-22: written to look two
# levels down it found nothing at all, the call opened with no brief and no record_answers tool,
# and the model invented a customer's name on a live call rather than reading the one it held.

helpers:
  briefIn:
    args: [signal]
    body: >-
      return (() => {
        const flat = o => (o && typeof o === 'object' && !Array.isArray(o)) ? Object.values(o) : [];
        const l1 = flat(signal);
        const l2 = l1.reduce((acc, v) => acc.concat(flat(v)), []);
        const l3 = l2.reduce((acc, v) => acc.concat(flat(v)), []);
        const found = l1.concat(l2).concat(l3)
          .map(v => (v && typeof v === 'object') ? (v.requirements || v) : null)
          .filter(r => r && Array.isArray(r.fields));
        return found.length ? found[0] : null;
      })()

  # THE NAMES ONLY. A task's `fields` are sometimes plain strings and sometimes objects with a
  # name; what a tool's enum needs is the words either way.
  fieldNamesIn:
    args: [brief]
    body: >-
      return ((brief || {}).fields || [])
        .map(f => (typeof f === 'string' ? f
          : String((f || {}).name || (f || {}).field || (f || {}).key || '')))
        .filter(n => n)
shared.tools.yaml:
# The OpenAI Responses tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does NOT belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it
# does not belong copied into every node either. It belongs here: shared by every OpenAI
# node, imported whole.
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#     maxTurns: 5            # local keys layer on top and win
#
# When OpenAI changes how a function call is expressed, exactly one file changes.
# NO SDK. This is the wire format, described as data.

# How ONE tool is offered to the model. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
#
# `strict: false`, said out loud. Left unsaid, the Responses API defaults it to true and
# REWRITES the schema to fit: every property joins `required`, and `minLength` is enforced by
# the decoder. A briefed component's contract is the opposite, `required: []`, "any subset is
# a valid call" (core/markdown/compile.ts). Under the default the model could not open a task
# without writing every field, so it asked the guest questions instead (SAB transfer,
# 2026-09-15, read back from the stored responses). The server referees each call anyway.
# `output_schema` when the tool declares what it returns (a component's `outputs` block, MCP
# `outputSchema`): the model reads what comes back before it calls.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters, strict: false,
           ...(tool.outputSchema ? { output_schema: tool.outputSchema } : {}) }
toolsInto: tools

# How a call ARRIVES in the stream.
call:
  match: response.output_item.done
  when: "return response.item.type === 'function_call'"
  id: "return response.item.call_id"
  name: "return response.item.name"
  arguments: "return response.item.arguments"

# How ONE result goes BACK. `call` is { id, name, output }.
result: >-
  return { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output }
resultsInto: input

# Always auto: which tool to reach for is carried by the tool DESCRIPTIONS, never by
# forcing a choice.
choiceInto: tool_choice
choice: auto

# NO `continuity` HERE, and that is deliberate. How a turn reaches the one before it is a
# per-node CHOICE on this vendor, not one wire format, because OpenAI offers two and
# REFUSES both at once:
#
#   previous_response_id   chains response to response. A new id every turn, known only
#                          after the turn ends. Declared by OpenAIStream, and since
#                          2026-08-23 by OpenAIAgent too — which now outlives a single
#                          execution by REMEMBERING that id (continuity.remember) rather
#                          than by holding a durable one.
#   conversation           a durable id, minted once and named on every turn, with the API
#                          keeping the history. No caller today.
#
# Sending both is `mutually_exclusive_parameters`, a hard 400 (confirmed against the live
# API 2026-08-12). So a node that names a conversation must NOT inherit continuity, and
# this file cannot decide for both. Each declares its own, next to the reason it chose it.

files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE WALK, IN TURNS (packages/docs/nodes/calls-that-loop.md, `repeat`). A turn is two calls:
#
#   choices  the engine's route of the choices one step from the ids, over `scope.engineUrl`
#            (loopback). Turn one opens `signal.ids`; every later turn opens what the turn
#            before chose.
#   decide   one plain OpenAI call, no tools, whose reply is bound to a schema: the ids to open
#            next, or the answer with its sources.
#
# ONE REPLY IS ONE JSON OBJECT: the model's last text piece is read, never the pieces joined
# (2026-09-13: a reply in two pieces read as two objects run together and failed to parse).
#
# THE WALK REMEMBERS IN ITS OWN NOTES, NOT IN A RESENT HISTORY (2026-09-13: chaining each turn
# to the one before resent every earlier menu, most of a question's 25,000 tokens). Each reply
# carries `notes`, what it has found and opened so far; the next turn sends the question, those
# notes and only the rows just opened.
#
# IT CANNOT RUN FOREVER. It ends when a reply answers or opens nothing (`until`), when a turn
# repeats the one before (`stuckAfterRepeats`), at `config.maxTurns`, and at the platform's 20
# whatever the config says. Every call has a ceiling on its output. The ids asked for are cut
# to five, the route's own bound.

- name: walk
  repeat:
    calls:
      - name: choices
        method: GET
        transport: json
        url: >-
          return scope.engineUrl + '/dictionary/choices?ids=' + encodeURIComponent(
            String(previous ? JSON.parse(previous.decide.output.filter(i => i.type === 'message').flatMap(i => i.content).filter(p => p.type === 'output_text').map(p => p.text).slice(-1).join('')).open : signal.ids)
              .split(',').map(x => x.trim()).filter(x => x).slice(0, 5).join(','))
            + '&q=' + encodeURIComponent(signal.question)
        timeoutMs: 60000

      - name: decide
        method: POST
        url: { $ref: endpoints#responses }
        credential:
          scheme: bearer
          token: "{{ credentials.openAICredential.apiKey }}"
        body: >-
          return {
            model: config.model,
            // TODAY'S DATE LAST, as every model call carries it: "latest" and "most recent" need a today.
            instructions: String(config.instructions || '') + '\n\nToday is ' + Date.iso(Date.now()).split('T')[0] + '.',
            input: [{
              role: 'user',
              content: 'Question: ' + signal.question + '\n\n'
                + (previous
                    ? 'Your notes so far:\n' + String(JSON.parse(previous.decide.output.filter(i => i.type === 'message').flatMap(i => i.content).filter(p => p.type === 'output_text').map(p => p.text).slice(-1).join('')).notes || '') + '\n\n'
                    : '')
                + (calls.choices.items.length
                    ? 'Opened now:\n' + JSON.stringify(calls.choices.items)
                    : 'Nothing was found for those ids. Choose only from ids you have been shown.')
            }],
            reasoning: { effort: config.reasoning || 'low' },
            max_output_tokens: 8000,
            store: false,
            text: {
              verbosity: 'low',
              format: {
                type: 'json_schema',
                name: 'step',
                strict: true,
                schema: {
                  type: 'object',
                  additionalProperties: false,
                  required: ['open', 'answer', 'sources', 'why', 'notes', 'caveat'],
                  properties: {
                    open: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'The ids to open next, at most five. Empty when answering.' },
                    answer: { type: ['string', 'null'], description: 'The answer, only from words read. Null while still walking or when there is none.' },
                    sources: {
                      type: 'array',
                      items: {
                        type: 'object',
                        additionalProperties: false,
                        required: ['id', 'page', 'quote'],
                        properties: {
                          id: { type: 'string' },
                          page: { type: ['string', 'null'] },
                          quote: { type: 'string', description: 'The exact words the answer rests on.' }
                        }
                      }
                    },
                    why: { type: 'string', description: 'One sentence: why these ids, or why this answer.' },
                    caveat: { type: ['string', 'null'], description: 'When you answer and another document you were shown may give a different answer, say which in one sentence (its title, and what may differ). Null when none may, and while still walking.' },
                    notes: { type: 'string', description: 'Everything the answer needs that you have found so far, with its id, pages and exact words, and the ids you have opened and the other ids you were shown that may still hold it. Carried to your next turn in place of what you read, so keep what matters: at most 1500 characters.' }
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        timeoutMs: 120000
        retry:
          attempts: 3
          backoff: exponential
          on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 520, 522, 524]
        transport: json
        error:
          when: "return !!response.error"
          message: "return response.error.message"

    until: >-
      return [JSON.parse(calls.decide.output.filter(i => i.type === 'message').flatMap(i => i.content).filter(p => p.type === 'output_text').map(p => p.text).slice(-1).join(''))].some(step => step.answer !== null || !step.open.length)
    maxTurns: "{{ config.maxTurns }}"
    stuckAfterRepeats: 2
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [model]

  properties:
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: GPT-5.6 model that chooses where to go and answers
      enum: { $ref: models#enum }
      enumNames: { $ref: models#enumNames }
      # LUNA, NOT THE PLATFORM DEFAULT. A walk is many small calls, one per turn, and a
      # question opens several documents: the volume is the cost, not any one call. Choosing
      # from a menu of headings and quoting what was read is small-tier work.
      default: gpt-5.6-terra
      resolve: modelTier

    instructions:
      type: string
      title: Instructions
      description: >-
        How to walk and when to stop. The default is written for any tree; add to it only
        what is particular to the questions this node will be asked.
      default: >-
        You answer one question by walking a tree of rows, one step at a time. Each turn you
        are shown the rows you opened. Each row has its own face (title, description, whenToUse)
        and its choices: what it belongs to (up), what is inside it (down), and what sits beside
        it (sideways), each with an id, a title, a description, a whenToUse and pages. A row may
        also carry found: the parts anywhere under it whose faces best match the question, each
        with its id and how near it came: a hint at which row to look in, never the list of what
        is there. At the bottom of the tree a row also
        carries its words: text, or a table's rows. Choose the ids
        to open next, at most five, only from ids you have been shown. Open every one that could
        hold the answer, up to five, never the fewest. A found part names the row worth looking
        in: open THAT ROW and read what is inside it (down), because found ranks faces by
        wording and the words of a question are rarely the words of a title. Then open the parts
        it names. You have not answered from a row until you have read its own words, and you may
        never say a row does not hold something until you have seen what is inside it. You do not see earlier turns again: keep in your notes what you
        found, where, and the ids still worth opening. Answer only from text or rows you have read, never from a title
        alone, and give every source: its id, its pages, and the exact words the answer rests
        on. Open nothing only when you are answering.
        When the rows give more than one answer (for different variants, dates or sources), give
        each, labelled with the row it comes from and its pages, and never choose one silently:
        whoever asked decides which applies. Before
        answering, check the other found parts that could hold a different answer. If nothing read holds the answer and nothing left to open looks likely to, answer
        null and open nothing.
      ui:field: template

    maxTurns:
      type: number
      title: Most turns
      description: >-
        The most branches opened in a row before the walk stops without an answer. The
        platform stops every walk at 20, whatever this says.
      default: 8
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 20

    reasoning:
      type: string
      title: Reasoning
      description: How much the model thinks before each choice.
      enum: [none, low, medium, high]
      default: low
ui:order: [model, instructions, maxTurns, reasoning]
files.interface.yaml:
# Both inputs are WIRED: the caller knows the question and where it is standing.
inputs:
  - name: question
    type: string
    description: The one question to answer

  - name: ids
    type: string
    description: The ids to start from, comma-separated (one to five), such as the row the caller holds

outputs:
  - name: answer
    type: string
    description: The answer, or null when the walk found none

  - name: sources
    type: array
    description: What the answer rests on, each with its id, its pages and the exact words

  - name: path
    type: array
    description: Every turn in order, what was opened, what was chosen next and why. The lineage of the answer

  - name: caveat
    type: string
    description: When another document may give a different answer, which one and what may differ; null when none may

  - name: stopped
    type: string
    description: Why the walk ended, until (answered or gave up), maxTurns or stuck

  - name: usage
    type: object
    description: Token usage over every turn

credentials:
  - name: openAICredential
    required: true
    displayName: OpenAI API
files.node.yaml:
type: OpenAISearchDetail
kind: PromiseNode

name: GPT-5 Search Detail
category: AI
color: "#2F6F66"

description: >-
  Answer one question from a tree of rows by opening one branch at a time: each turn reads the
  choices one step from the rows it opened, and the model opens more or answers, with the path
  it took and the words each answer rests on.

whenToUse: >-
  Pick when the answer to one question sits somewhere inside a large object (a deal and its
  documents, a long document and its sections, a table's rows) and sending the whole of it to a
  model would be too long or too costly: the model reads titles and descriptions to choose where
  to go, and reads text only where it chose to. The wrong choice when the content is already
  short enough to hand over whole, or when many questions are asked of one text at once. Wire the
  question and the ids to start from in as inputs.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13).
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A model chooses each turn, so the same question may walk a different path.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# The ids are a WORKSPACE's own rows: paste the id of a row from the Content Library (a long
# document is the case this node exists for) and ask a question its text answers.
testData:
  config:
    model: gpt-5.6-terra
    maxTurns: 6

  inputs:
    question: What was the fund's net return for the month?
    ids: paste-a-row-id

  expect:
    # Proves the walk ended by its own rule, and kept its path.
    stopped: "return ['until', 'maxTurns', 'stuck'].includes(output.stopped)"
    path: "return output.path.length >= 1"
